manifesto.titulo: A brand is forged with care. And it has to stay alive in every piece of work.
manifesto.lead: Brennimark, in Icelandic, is the fire brand: the sign burned in with iron that said who something belonged to. The English word brand comes from the same idea of burning.
manifesto.p1: It has been more than forty years of design and art direction. In almost all of them, the same difficulty came back: the deadline running, the manual in a long PDF, the files scattered across folders and the answer that took too long to arrive.
manifesto.pull1: Brennimark is the help I always wanted to have.
manifesto.p2: A brand is born from the careful work of the people who create it: the drawing of the symbol, the weight of each letter, the exact color, the space around it. Then it goes on to many hands: the agency, the supplier, the printer, whoever has just joined the team. Each one carries the idea forward.
manifesto.p3: Brennimark brings together the manual as the studio designed it, the up-to-date materials and the guidance the brand gains over time. Vini helps find the answer, with the source, so that time goes back to what matters: thinking, researching and creating.
manifesto.p4: A living brand is not a rigid brand. It evolves, gains new guidance and sometimes reinvents itself, and everyone needs to follow the current version.
manifesto.p5: We respect the authorship of those who created it and the decision of those who apply it. We don't invent rules, and we say clearly when there is no safe answer.
manifesto.pull2: Forged with care. Alive in every piece of work.

fonts.titulo: The font manager built for people who work with brands.
fonts.lead: Local library, reliable activation and fonts organized by brand and by client. The goal is to be the best font manager for art directors, agencies and studios.

fonts.devCorpo: Nothing on this list is in the beta. It is on the roadmap, in this order of priority, and only appears on the site as ready after being tested.
fonts.compNota: Highlighted = whoever has the advantage on that row. FontBase data comes from its public website as of Oct 14, 2026 and may have changed; we have not tested its app in depth. Today FontBase has more features ready and runs on Linux. Our bet is the font tied to the brand: a kit per client, activation with conflict control and the brand manual in the same place.
fonts.s1: Only the first 50 approved requests, on macOS and Windows. Each invitation lasts 90 days. It may have flaws and change. Linux comes later.
fonts.s2: The installer is not signed yet. macOS and Windows will warn that the source is not verified; the questions section shows the step by step.
fonts.s3: Coming soon, with a signed installer and an annual license. When the 90 days are over, those who tested move to the paid version on launch terms, to be announced.
fonts.pedidoFeito: Request received. We will review it and write to you, in the order of the requests. There are 50 spots.
fonts.r1d: Catalog on your computer. Works without internet and without an account; network features, when they arrive, come turned off.
fonts.r2d: Point to a folder and Fonts catalogs TTF, OTF and TTC/OTC collections. It doesn't copy, install or delete anything.
fonts.r3d: Each file is recognized by its fingerprint (SHA-256). An exact duplicate is found even under a different name.
fonts.r4d: Whenever you want, it keeps a managed copy of the font. Removal goes to a recoverable area; there is no permanent deletion.
fonts.r5d: Temporary activation on macOS and Windows, with name-conflict control and recovery if the app closes midway.
fonts.r6d: A family's styles stay together, searchable by family, weight, style and variable-font axes.
fonts.r7d: Glyphs by Unicode block, OpenType features (ligatures, small caps, alternates), variable axes and a Playground with CSS.
fonts.r8d: Organize by project and by client. A kit gathers a brand's fonts to activate them all at once.
fonts.r9d: Fonts follows folders and notices what came in, changed or disappeared. An offline folder doesn't turn into lost fonts.
fonts.r10d: Free-form labels and collections that build themselves from rules (for example, sans with Bold weight and italic).
fonts.r11d: Compares shapes measured in the file itself and shows similar alternatives within your library.
fonts.r12d: The About screen generates a support summary with version and system. It never includes paths, font names or clients.

fonts.dev2: Google Fonts, optional and off by default
fonts.dev3: Synchronization between computers through the Brennimark account
fonts.dev4: Brennimark account and license inside the app, and automatic updates

fonts.c2f: Included in the Brennimark subscription; standalone annual (price to be announced).

fonts.q1: Why the system warning when installing?
fonts.a1: The warning appears because this beta does not yet have a digital distribution signature (Apple and Microsoft charge for certificates, which we will purchase before the official launch). It does not indicate a problem with the file: macOS and Windows are only warning that they don't know the author. The installer comes directly from us, with the checksum so you can confirm that the file is the same.
fonts.q2: How do I open it on a Mac?
fonts.a2: When you open it for the first time, macOS warns that it cannot verify the app. Go to System Settings, Privacy & Security, scroll to the message about Brennimark Fonts and choose Open Anyway. The beta is for Macs with an Apple chip; Intel has not been tested yet.
fonts.q3: How do I open it on Windows?
fonts.a3: SmartScreen shows Windows protected your PC. Click More info and then Run anyway. The installer is per user and does not ask for administrator permission. Tested on Windows 11.
fonts.q4: Do my fonts go to any server?
fonts.a4: No. The catalog, the Vault copies, the collections and the kits stay on your computer. The support summary never carries a font name, path or client.
fonts.q5: Can I trust my working library to a beta?
fonts.a5: Fonts doesn't delete or alter the originals. Even so, it is a beta: start with a test folder and keep your usual backup.
fonts.q6: Is the beta paid? How long is it valid?
fonts.a6: It isn't paid, and it is by invitation, limited to the first 50 approved requests. Once you request access, we review it and send the installer; the trial is valid for 90 days. After that, you need to move to the paid version, which will be ready by then.
fonts.q7: What if the 50 spots run out?
fonts.a7: The beta does not open spots beyond the 50. Whoever is left out can ask for the launch notice, at the top of the page, and use Fonts included in the Brennimark subscription or in the standalone version, when it is released.
fonts.a8: Soon, with no fixed date. The paid version is a one-year license, with updates and new versions during its validity; after that, it renews. Whoever subscribes to Brennimark already receives Fonts. Whoever tests the beta gets launch terms, which we will announce before any charge.
